title: Set the viewport unit and the contrast floor first
intent: Fix the two measurable properties that decide whether the page is usable before any layout work starts.
when_to_use: any page with a full height section
any page with text or controls over imagery, tinted panels, or brand colour
when_not_to_use: the artifact never uses a full height section and every surface is a pair of known neutral tokens, where the floor is already satisfied and needs no per section pass
the artifact renders inside a fixed height frame the host controls, so the viewport unit is not the artifact's choice
rules: full height sections use 100dvh, never 100vh, and a literal 100vh in the stylesheet is a defect
body text reaches at least 4.5 to 1 against its background and large text at least 3 to 1, measured on rendered values
text over imagery sits on a real scrim and the ratio is checked against the lightest region the text covers
a colour that cannot be resolved from the token set is reported as unknown, never assumed to pass
trade_off: A hard contrast floor rules out subtle grey on grey styling and forces scrims that dull the imagery, which is the price of the text being readable.
failure_mode: The ratio is checked on token values while the page renders a lighter overlay, so the audit passes on paper and fails on screen.

example.brief: Agency portfolio with a full height hero photograph and a caption over it.
example.ruling: Hero height is 100dvh on a solid scrim token, the caption measures 4.6 to 1 against the lightest column it covers, and the image treatment is chosen to meet the floor rather than the floor being waived.
